results.title: Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty
results.content: The Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty (INF Treaty) was an arms control treaty between the United States and the Soviet Union (and its successor state, the Russian Federation). On 8 March 2019, the Foreign Ministry of Ukraine "Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ukraine)") announced that since the United States and Russia had both pulled out of the treaty, it now had the right to develop intermediate-range missiles, citing Russian aggression against Ukraine as a serious threat to the European continent, and the presence of Russian Iskander-M nuclear-capable missile systems in Russian-annexed Crimea.

results.title: Russia Suspends New START and Increases Nuclear Risks
results.content: In a lengthy and fiery speech on February 21, 2023, Russian president Vladimir Putin announced the suspension of Russia’s participation in the 2010 New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START). It also followed an announcement on January 31, 2023, by the U.S. State Department that Russia was in violation of New START. It’s also something the rest of the world expects of us.” This suggests the United States will continue to abide by the New START limits and pursue arms control and other risk reduction measures, even without a willing partner in Moscow. But whether the United States and Russia revive New START, negotiate a new agreement, or resort to informal risk reduction mechanisms, the future of arms control is perilous.
